Looking at each square with side length 1 (coordinates with bottom-left at (0,0)):

**Square I:** Lines: diagonal from (0,1) to (1,0): y = 1−x; line from (0,0) to top midpoint (½,1): y = 2x. Intersection: x = 1/3, y = 2/3. Shaded triangle has base = bottom side (1) and height 2/3: area = ½·1·(2/3) = **1/3**.

**Square II:** Lines: diagonal from (0,1) to (1,0): y = 1−x; line from (0,0) to right midpoint (1,½): y = x/2. Intersection: x = 2/3, y = 1/3. Shaded triangle has base = bottom side (1) and height 1/3: area = ½·1·(1/3) = **1/6**.

**Square III:** Lines: from (0,1) to bottom midpoint (½,0): y = 1−2x; from (0,0) to right midpoint (1,½): y = x/2. Intersection: x = 2/5, y = 1/5. Shaded triangle has base = left side (1) and height (horizontal distance) 2/5: area = ½·1·(2/5) = **1/5**.

**Comparison:** 1/6 < 1/5 < 1/3, so S_II < S_III < S_I.

\boxed{C}
